# Same-day completed DAILY accounting refresh

This source-only review accepts the parent's narrow correction conditionally on these exact fences. It introduces no new day slot, signing permission, V1 behavior, scheduler kind or persisted encoding.

After original recovery completes with empty reason, the selected DAILY scheduler may dispatch its existing `daily` kind when either original `dailyDue` is true or `completedDailyRefreshDue` is true. The latter requires original selected Version2 state/config, valid nondecreasing actual wall time, exact cursor equality with the current UTC date, and the configured UTC minute reached. The private immutable scheduler mode still selects the daily Store; a shaped State is not owner authority. The dispatch choice is recomputed under the original mutex and the exact durable Attempt.AdmittedDay is carried to the original Store operation.

`Store.RefreshCompletedDaily(ctx, admittedDay)` must be strict DAILY and writable. Under the original gate, perform the unchanged complete row/source audit and actual clock sample; require `date(sampledMS)==admittedDay` and original audited `head.LastDay>=date(sampledMS)` plus `head.PendingBatch==0` before backend, credit import or persisted effects. The gate remains held. Since original normal preparation can reach its signer only below `head.LastDay<day`, this route cannot create a batch even if called directly. The entire unchanged ready frontier is inspected; whole source import remains atomic. Exact pending recovery and historical original transaction checks remain intact. A rollover refusal cannot convert this operation into tomorrow's new payment. It returns the distinct `ErrDailyRefreshExpired`, mapped to the existing retryable scheduler unavailable classification; the cursor stays unchanged and the next wake may admit the proper new-day due. A final report may observe the next day but retains the original completed day, as existing finish/audit already permits.

No actionable contradiction was found in the proposal with these fences. An already future LastDay also cannot license signing; ordinary clock/header validation remains applicable. The predicate is eligibility only: existing admitted-revision, next-wake, owner/context and full-audit checks may still refuse it. The upper timestamp case in the table intentionally does not promise that nextWake can be represented.

`cases.json` is a small hand-derived table from this predicate. It is not generated by or copied from Go output. ISO instants can be parsed to milliseconds by consumers; `now_ms`/`previous_ms` are used only for scalar clock edges. Its invalid/mixed-version rows are conditional pure refusal controls, not claims that malformed scheduler states pass the original decoder. Every row also records the unchanged original new-payment due result to make non-overlap visible. A same-day replay must keep DailyCursor unchanged; a Store rollover refusal must have zero backend/import/signing/broadcast/commit effects.

The Path B actual remains held until root implements and qualifies this correction. No runtime, producer or Go execution occurred in this review.
